independence_caveat: Same model family as the other reviewers; agreement is reading consistency, not independent validation.

findings.finding: C1 is falsifiable at the corpus boundary, not by a cosmological interpretation. The word realized must mean that each exact Gamma form occurs in the pinned normative source and executable implementation with declared units and parameter names; listing three equations is weaker than establishing three realized implementations.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 99-107 and 139-149, corpus layering and the three response forms.
findings.test: Blindly inventory the pinned package PDFs and source files, extract Gamma_A, Gamma_B, and Gamma_C, substitute SI dimensions, and run each package's supplied example or unit test. Fail the realization part of C1 if any form is prose-only, absent from executable code, or differs from the stated expression.
findings.reasoning: The raw object is the versioned source artifact, so no cosmological model or standard-model interpretation is needed. A direct artifact audit can falsify realization while leaving mere textual mention intact.

findings.finding: C2 combines a provenance statement with a non-selection statement. The simplest raw-data challenge to the latter is a matched, held-out comparison of Gamma_A, Gamma_B, and Gamma_C on the same measured response data with common normalization and nuisance treatment. A decisive predeclared selection would falsify the claim that no empirical selection has been demonstrated for that scope, but it would not by itself prove or disprove the historical genealogy phrase shape bifurcation.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 159-166, where the bifurcation and absence of demonstrated selection are asserted.
findings.test: Freeze one raw-observation sample, the response reconstruction, units, normalizations, nuisance priors, regime cuts, and a likelihood-ratio or equivalent predictive-score statistic before viewing residuals. Evaluate all three forms on a held-out subset. Treat a reproducible threshold crossing as evidence for selection, not as proof of a maturation chain.
findings.reasoning: Raw measured response data can discriminate numerical predictions without importing any cosmological limit. A null comparison only leaves the selection unresolved; it cannot establish the genealogical label on its own.

findings.finding: C3 has a direct formal falsification route, but no observational test is meaningful until Gamma_B is normalized. The vulnerable point is the residual square-root density dimension: an authoritative prefactor, reference scale, or prior nondimensionalization would remove the asserted defect, whereas merely relabelling rho would not.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 141-149, including the dimensional qualification on Gamma_B.
findings.test: Perform a source-level dimensional audit in SI units on Gamma_B, its entropy derivative, and every downstream use. Fail C3 if the authoritative source or implementation supplies a valid reference scale or prefactor that makes the response dimensionally consistent before comparison; otherwise retain the defect and block raw-data fitting of the unnormalized form.
findings.reasoning: Dimensions and normalization are properties of the written equations and implementation, not of a preferred cosmology. The raw signal cannot adjudicate two forms that do not yet have commensurate units.

findings.finding: C4 is a status claim and becomes empirically vulnerable only if B and B+ make distinguishable, normalized predictions. A raw-data comparison can support selection of one form, but it cannot automatically turn the author's companion-upgrade label into physical supersession; the selection rule, common nuisance treatment, and normalization must be frozen first.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 154-161, which call B+ a declared companion upgrade and leave supersession unestablished.
findings.test: Predeclare a common-unit, held-out likelihood or predictive-score comparison of B and B+ on raw response observables, with all shared and form-specific parameters frozen or assigned fixed priors. A reproducible superiority criterion may establish empirical selection; indistinguishable predictions leave the upgrade and supersession claims unresolved.
findings.reasoning: No standard-model interpretation is required. The raw signal can test different numerical predictions, not the semantic word upgrade or an unrecorded author-intent relation.

findings.finding: C5 leaves the Gamma-shape axis without a discriminator. Calling it an open selection is descriptive, but it is not yet a falsifiable validation axis: any later choice among Gamma_A, Gamma_B, and Gamma_C after an anomaly is seen can be post hoc. The missing discriminator is a substantive gap independent of the E-axis test.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 163-187 and 214-217, especially the explicit statement that the Gamma-shape axis has no preregistered discriminator.
findings.test: Before inspecting residuals, freeze a raw-observation sample, a common response reconstruction, Gamma normalization, all nuisance priors, regime boundaries, pooling rule, and one model-comparison statistic. Apply Gamma_A, Gamma_B, and Gamma_C to held-out measured response data. A later form choice is a falsification result only if it passes that predeclared comparison; otherwise the axis remains taxonomy rather than physics.
findings.reasoning: The test uses measured signals and explicit calibration choices, not a standard-model reading. The manuscript itself distinguishes this axis from the proposed E-axis, so the E-axis discriminator cannot be used as a proxy for Gamma-shape selection.

findings.finding: The two square roots are syntactically in different variables, but C6 risks upgrading syntactic distinction into physical independence. The simplest check is a symbolic dependency and identifiability test: if the derivation forces alpha_E and the Gamma-shape choice to be linked, or if the raw data identify only their product, they are not two independently selectable physical axes even though the formulas look different.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 168-172, which distinguish the E exponent from the density dependence and state that physical independence is not demonstrated.
findings.test: Trace units, parameters, and equations from the source actions to both observables, then fit the crossed combinations of alpha_E and Gamma form to the same raw data with shared nuisance parameters. Reject the independent-axis reading if the formal map or the data impose a one-to-one relation or leave only a non-identifiable combination.
findings.reasoning: This test does not assume which cosmology is correct. It asks whether the two choices are mathematically and observationally separable; the manuscript currently claims only organizational separation.

findings.finding: KC1 has the skeleton of a conditional falsifier, but its operational predicates are not frozen by the stated threshold alone. Robust, bias-controlled, preferred, significantly, diverse systems, the pooling rule, the statistic, and the relevant acceleration or regime domain are undefined in the criterion. Without those locks, >=5 sigma is a nominal label that can be obtained or removed by post hoc choices rather than a reproducible raw-signal test.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 192-196, the current KC1 wording and its conditional >=5 sigma statement.
findings.test: Before opening the data, freeze the raw data release and sample cuts; define the linear and square-root screening functions; freeze a0 and all normalization conventions; specify distance, inclination, gas, mass-to-light and covariance treatment; define the statistic, sigma conversion, per-system versus pooled aggregation, outlier rule, and acceleration/regime boundaries; then run the blind comparison on held-out systems. Only a result crossing that exact predeclared rule can conditionally falsify E proportional to sqrt(g) within the stated scope.
findings.reasoning: The test compares measured galaxy signals directly and does not take any standard-model interpretation as ground truth. The issue is not whether 5 sigma is mathematically possible, but whether the event that counts as 5 sigma was fixed before seeing the residuals.

findings.finding: The provenance gap is directly testable, and null metadata is not the same as a reproduced null or 5 sigma result. The simplest check is to retrieve the raw SPARC inputs and the claimed analysis artifact and rerun the exact comparison. If no data, code, commit, cuts, likelihood, and output trace exist, the nominal exclusion remains unsubstantiated; if they reproduce, the provenance gap closes.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 194-198, especially the null Delta chi2/significance and no-new-fit statement.
findings.test: Reconstruct the claimed fit from the raw data release and pinned analysis artifact. Record the exact data hash, selection, nuisance configuration, statistic, Delta chi2, sigma conversion, and per-system and pooled outputs. Treat an absent or non-reproducible provenance chain as failure to establish the >=5 sigma exclusion, not as evidence for either screening form.
findings.reasoning: This is a raw-data and provenance readback, independent of cosmological interpretation. It directly distinguishes an executed result from an inherited label or external citation.

findings.finding: Freezing a0 is necessary but not sufficient for the SPARC/RAR discriminator. The stated candidates and anti-shopping rule do not also freeze the nuisance path from raw signals to baryonic and dynamical quantities: mass-to-light ratios, distances, inclinations, gas treatment, sample and radial cuts, covariance, priors, and fit statistic can absorb or create the apparent distinction. The discriminator is therefore not operational if a0 is the only explicitly frozen quantity.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 214-220, especially the proposed Axis 1 paragraph and its a0-only freeze language.
findings.test: Freeze the exact raw SPARC release, galaxy inclusion and radial cuts, distance and inclination inputs, gas maps, mass-to-light priors, covariance/error model, nuisance optimization, and fit statistic before the blind retrodiction. Hold exactly one author-frozen a0 fixed, run once, and report residuals and the predeclared score without post hoc nuisance changes. Any remaining tunability invalidates the claimed discrimination even if a0 itself is frozen.
findings.reasoning: These are measurement and reconstruction choices, not commitments to the standard model. A single frozen scale cannot prevent researcher degrees of freedom elsewhere in the raw-signal pipeline.

findings.finding: A non-unit GW/EM luminosity-distance ratio is a raw observational comparison, but the inequality alone is not an EFC discriminator. To test C10 as stated, the coupling parameters and field normalization must be frozen together with source association, waveform and electromagnetic calibration, redshift, selection, lensing, peculiar-velocity treatment, and the likelihood. The manuscript's caution that dL_GW not equal to dL_EM is generic until this freeze is therefore the correct vulnerability boundary.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 214-221, the proposed siren test and its unfrozen coupling parameters.
findings.test: Pre-register a multi-messenger event set and a likelihood for dL_GW/dL_EM, freeze alpha, phi0, phi(z), field normalization, calibration and selection corrections, and compare the frozen EFC curve against equality and other propagation laws on held-out events. A non-unit ratio without that comparison rejects only the equality baseline, not uniquely EFC.
findings.reasoning: The test treats equality as a comparison hypothesis, not as a privileged standard-model truth. Distinguishability comes from the frozen EFC prediction and alternatives, not from the existence of an anomaly alone.

findings.finding: C11 is a negative scope claim and needs an artifact-level audit rather than a cosmological test. A clean reconstruction can test whether this manuscript ran a new fit, but absence of a fit in the text does not prove absence of an unreported external validation or inherited output. The claim is vulnerable wherever its negative statements are not tied to commits, commands, data hashes, and logs.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 223-234, the explicit list of analyses and validations not performed here.
findings.test: Build and inspect the frozen tree in a clean environment, enumerate every executed analysis command and output hash, and compare the manuscript's citations with the source-package provenance. Separately require an independent pipeline and new data if the phrase independent validation is ever changed; an internal replay cannot falsify that distinction.
findings.reasoning: The raw evidence is the repository, build log, and data provenance. No interpretation of galaxy dynamics or cosmological limits is needed to test what work was actually executed.

findings.finding: C12 has a byte-level falsification test with two separable subclaims. Repeated clean builds test byte-for-byte identity; the raw build logs test the absence of Overfull, Underfull, and float-placement warnings. A differing hash caused by timestamp or trailer metadata is direct evidence that achieved reproducibility is not yet present, while any warning falsifies the clean-build subclaim.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 344-346, which describe the reproducibility limitation and current warning status.
findings.test: Run the stated build twice from the identical frozen source and container, save raw stdout/stderr and PDF bytes, compute both hashes, and compare the logs for the three warning classes. Repeat after suppressing nondeterministic metadata only as a diagnostic; do not call the original build byte-reproducible unless its original hashes match.
findings.reasoning: The raw signals are bytes and compiler logs. This test is wholly independent of any cosmological model or preferred interpretation.

findings.finding: C13 is not yet an operationally falsifiable regime claim. The MOND-like and LCDM-like labels need pre-defined boundaries in directly measured variables, a frozen transition rule, and a held-out prediction. If a regime is named only after an anomaly is observed or is defined by the residual it is meant to explain, the result is a gaps argument rather than physics. The cited Review status passage is prior-review text and cannot supply independent evidence for the ontology.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 294-304, Review status regime interpretation; this region is explicitly treated as prior-review text, not independent evidence.
findings.test: Before inspecting the anomaly, freeze numerical regime boundaries and a classifier using only measured acceleration, density, scale, redshift, or other explicitly recorded observables; define the transition tolerance and pooling rule; calibrate on one set and evaluate on held-out raw observations. Require the same boundaries to predict both labelled behaviours and any transition. Post hoc boundaries fail the regime test.
findings.reasoning: Neither MOND nor LCDM is used as ground truth here; the test asks whether the labels correspond to a predeclared, repeatable pattern in raw signals. Without frozen boundaries, the ontology can accommodate any residual after the fact.

findings.finding: C14 is a corpus-scope claim and is falsifiable by a direct registry audit, not by cosmological data. The vulnerable point is whether the three broader persistent identifiers are actually enumerated, accessible, and included under the same provenance rule rather than appearing only as an informal extension beyond Table 1. The inclusion boundary must be explicit and reproducible.
findings.source: snapshot.tex lines 110-127 and 350-351, Table 1 and the corpus-provenance note distinguishing the six primary packages from broader cited packages.
findings.test: Parse every persistent identifier in the frozen manuscript and repository register, classify each as one of the six Table 1 packages or a broader cited package, and verify the records and roles for 31943361, 31348411, and 31348417. Fail the broad-scope part of C14 if any identifier is uncited, inaccessible, unpinned, or included only through an unenumerated review passage.
findings.reasoning: The raw evidence is the identifier registry and package records. This tests provenance scope directly and makes no assumption about which cosmological interpretation is correct.
